why: Shell cycle 1 (docs/v3/cycles/shell-1.md, P2 shell-1.22, P3 shell-1.20): two repo gates read `apps/playground/src/routes/cycle/**` as if a cycle route were a demo route, and a cycle brief forbids `packages/basalt-ui/**`. The quality matrix reads every route file (`packages/basalt-ui/tests/quality/matrix/routes.ts`), so a cycle that composes kit parts with known findings fails CI unless its PR adds `known.ts` lines in the package; this cycle did, against its brief. The route-file budget (`packages/basalt-ui/scripts/check-budgets/areas/playground.ts:15`) counts `routes/cycle/**`, which `apps/playground/src/budget.test.ts` leaves out, so the cycle could not add a layout route.
what: A cycle's routes and their waivers stay inside the cycle's own files.
owns: docs/v3/CYCLES.md (step 2: where a cycle's matrix waivers live)
docs/v3/issues/cycles/v3-cycle-*.json of cycles not yet filed (their owns line, only if CYCLES.md changes it)
change: The matrix keeps reading cycle routes (they are real composition evidence) and also reads waivers from `apps/playground/src/cycle/*/known.ts`, with the same `KnownFinding` shape and the same 'an entry that matched nothing fails the full run' rule; the `/cycle/state` and `/cycle/shell*` lines move there, each still naming its owner row. Or, if the architecture prefers, `CYCLES.md` step 2 allows a cycle PR its `known.ts` lines and nothing else under `packages/`; the PR says which and why. The route-file budget excludes `routes/cycle/` as `budget.test.ts` does.
commits: test: one commit in packages/basalt-ui; the waiver move and CYCLES.md in their own commits.
proof: make check; a matrix unit test that a waiver in a cycle folder covers its route's item.
acceptance: A cycle can add a route and its waivers without a file under `packages/basalt-ui/` (or CYCLES.md says it may touch exactly `known.ts`)
out_of_scope: Fixing the waived findings (their rows: v3-shell-1-visual, v3-shell-1-inner-nav, v3-state-1-visual).
